thread.title: iPhone supplier with major DFW presence acquired for $3.2B

author: Evan Hoopfer
title: iPhone supplier with major DFW presence acquired for $3.2B
text: – Staff Writer, Dallas Business Journal Nov 10, 2018, 1:58pm CST Finisar, the manufacturer that announced it was bringing 500 high-paying jobs to Sherman, Texas, last year, was acquired in a $3.2 billion deal, the company announced Friday. II-VI Inc. (NASDAQ: IIVI), based outside of Pittsburgh, agreed to pay Finisar Corp. (NASDAQ: FNSR) shareholders $15.60 per share in cash and 0.2218x shares of II-VI common stock , valued at $10.40 a share. The transaction values Finisar at $26.00 a share, a nearly 38-percent premium to Thursday's close. Finisar made waves last December when it announced it was repurposing an old facility in Sherman to make vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers, or VCSELs. The product is a key part of the new iPhones made by technology giant Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL). VCSELs are basically "really advanced technology that emits laser beams," said Jeff Williams , chief operating officer of Apple, at the time. They power things like Face ID, Animoji and Portrait mode selfies for the iPhone X. The city of Sherman offered an incentive package that totaled about $4.5 million to Finisar, which bought the 700,000-square-foot facility for $20 million last year. As of July, the company was half way through hiring 500 employees to the Sherman facility. Between Finisar and II-VI, the company will have more than 24,000 employees in 70 locations and the combined company will have annual revenue of $2.5 billion. – Staff Writer, Dallas Business Journal Nov 10, 2018, 1:58pm CST Deadline: Friday, November 30, 2018 2019 Minority Business Leader Awards Nominate today for our 12th annual Minority Business Leader Awards!
